jobs.description:
**“See It and Be It” Program Coordinator (Richmond Area)**

**STEAM the Streets | Part-Time Contract | 8-15 hours/week | November–March | $30/hour**

**About STEAM the Streets**

STEAM the Streets is a mission-driven organization that uses media, music, arts, and STEAM education to connect young people to careers and inspire them to see new possibilities for their futures.

**About the Role**

STEAM the Streets is seeking a highly organized, proactive **See It and Be It Richmond Area Program Coordinator** to support the delivery of our **See It and Be It** program with our partners at West Contra Costa Unified School District (WCCUSD) Department of College and Career.

This is a **part-time, project-based contract role** responsible for coordinating logistics, communication, and school-site readiness across four participating middle schools. The coordinator will help ensure that the program is organized and ready from initial school coordination through the February assembly week and early curriculum implementation.

The ideal candidate is organized, responsive, comfortable communicating with school staff, and able to manage multiple moving pieces with minimal supervision.

**About the See It and Be It Program**

**See It and Be It** is a career exploration program from STEAM the Streets that introduces middle school students to a range of STEAM careers through engaging classroom curriculum and real-world exposure. The program kicks off with our **“This Can Be You”** career exploration assemblies, followed by classroom-based career exploration that helps students discover new possibilities and pathways for their future.

**Key Responsibilities**

**Program Preparation & Coordination – November–January**

* Onboard with STEAM the Streets and review existing commitments, timelines, contacts, forms, and planning materials for the four participating schools.
* Establish and maintain communication with school administrators and teachers at each site.
* Schedule planning meetings and coordinate follow-up with each school.
* Coordinate deadlines and readiness activities leading up to the February assemblies.
* Ensure January deadlines are met for assembly forms, school site visits, technical checks, schedules, and final confirmations.
* Conduct site visits to assess assembly spaces and document logistics, including room setup, AV/technical needs, parking/loading, student capacity, and arrival procedures.
* Coordinate technical checks and communicate site-specific needs to the STEAM the Streets team.
* Maintain a master schedule and program logistics tracker for all four schools.
* Coordinate catering and materials for the professional development/training session.
* Support preparation and on-site logistics for the December train-the-trainer session for approximately 8–12 WCCUSD educators.
* Coordinate pre-program survey follow-up with participating teachers, ensuring teachers understand their role in distributing and completing student pre-surveys.

**This Can Be You Assembly Week – February 8-12**The coordinator will serve as the primary on-the-ground logistics support for STEAM the Streets during assembly week, ensuring each school is prepared and the team has what it needs to successfully deliver the assemblies.

Responsibilities include:

* Confirm final details with each school prior to arrival.
* Coordinate arrival times and access with school staff and the STEAM the Streets team.
* Ensure spaces, equipment, materials, and other site requirements are ready before each assembly.
* Help coordinate setup and troubleshoot logistical or technical issues that arise.
* Serve as the on-site point person for school logistics and communicate issues to the Founder / CEO as needed.
* Assist with breakdown and ensure materials and equipment are accounted for following each assembly.
* Complete daily follow-up and flag any outstanding issues or changes.

**Program Implementation – March**

* Maintain light-touch communication with participating educators as curriculum implementation begins.
* Follow up with teachers regarding student surveys and other program information.
* Conduct occasional school-site check-ins as needed.
* Track questions, issues, and follow-up items and escalate anything requiring STEAM the Streets leadership.
* Assist with collecting program feedback and basic participation information.

**Ideal Candidate**

* Highly organized and detail-oriented.
* Strong written and verbal communication skills.
* Comfortable communicating with school administrators, teachers, and education professionals.
* Reliable, responsive, and able to manage deadlines independently.
* Comfortable working on-site at schools and during program events.
* Able to anticipate logistical needs and troubleshoot problems calmly.
* Experience in education, youth programs, events, or nonprofit program coordination is a plus.
* Familiarity with WCCUSD or Richmond-area schools is helpful but not required.

**Contract Details**

**Position:** See It and Be It Richmond Area Program Coordinator**Type:** Part-Time Contract**Term:** November–March**Hours:** 8–15 hours per week, with a spike in hours during the February 8–12 assembly week**Rate:** $30/hour**Location:** Richmond area / Hybrid, with required in-person work at district and school sites during program activities**Reports to:** Founder / CEO, STEAM the Streets

**What Success Looks Like**

The coordinator keeps the **See It and Be It** program moving and makes sure each school is prepared, informed, and ready. By the time the STEAM the Streets team arrives at a school, the logistics should be confirmed, the site should be ready, and any potential issues should already be identified and communicated.

**Success means:**

* Each school is informed, prepared, and ready for its scheduled program activities.
* Assembly logistics are confirmed in advance, potential issues are identified early, and each assembly runs smoothly from arrival through breakdown.

**El Camino Health Medical Network is recruiting a talented Hospitalist Program Coordinator in Santa Clara County.**

Pay: $37.00 - $47.00/hour

Location: Los Gatos, CA

**El Camino Health Medical Network (ECHMN**) is a growing healthcare provider organization delivering high-quality, community-based ambulatory care across the Greater Silicon Valley. We are committed to coordinating care that meets the needs of the diverse communities we serve, while simplifying the healthcare experience for both patients and providers.

At ECHMN, we value collaboration, accountability, and innovation. Our teams work closely across disciplines to support physicians, improve access to care, and deliver a consistently high standard of service. We offer a supportive and engaging work environment where individuals are empowered to make an impact and contribute to meaningful growth.

If you are passionate about healthcare, driven by purpose, and eager to work in a collaborative, patient-centered organization, we invite you to explore a career with El Camino Health Medical Network.

  

**Summary**

The **Hospitalist Program** **Coordinator** provides operational, administrative, and physician support for the day-to-day activities of the Hospitalist Program. This position serves as a key liaison between hospitalist physicians and advanced practice providers (APPs), Medical Network leadership, hospital departments, Medical Staff Services, Human Resources, Finance, Payroll, and other operational partners.

The **Hospitalist Program** **Coordinator** supports physician and APP scheduling, onboarding and credentialing coordination, timekeeping and payroll processes, meeting administration, program communications, operational reporting, and ongoing program initiatives.

The position works closely with the Hospitalist Medical Director and operational leadership to support effective physician coverage, timely resolution of operational issues, and efficient coordination of hospitalist services.

  

**Hospitalist Program Operations**

* Provide day-to-day administrative and operational support for the Hospitalist Program.
* Serve as a primary point of contact for hospitalists and APPs regarding program operations, scheduling, administrative processes, and general program questions.
* Partner with the Hospitalist Medical Director and operational leadership to coordinate program priorities and activities.
* Identify operational issues and escalate matters requiring Medical Director or leadership review.
* Coordinate hospitalist program meetings, including scheduling, agendas, materials, meeting minutes, and follow-up items.

  

**Physician and APP Scheduling**

* Develop, maintain, and distribute physician and APP work schedules in partnership with the Medical Director and program leadership.
* Coordinate schedule changes, vacations, planned absences, and coverage needs.
* Assist with identifying coverage gaps and communicating open shifts to appropriate providers.
* Track schedule changes and ensure accurate communication to physicians, hospital departments, Medical Staff Services, Payroll, and other stakeholders as appropriate.
* Maintain accurate physician coverage and on-call schedules.
* Support provider schedule reconciliation and related reporting.

**Physician and APP Onboarding**

* Coordinate the administrative onboarding of new hospitalists and APPs.
* Work collaboratively with Physician Recruitment, Human Resources, Medical Staff Services, IT, hospital departments, and leadership to facilitate timely onboarding.
* Track credentialing, privileging, orientation, system access, badges, equipment, training, and other onboarding requirements.
* Coordinate orientation schedules and ensure providers receive necessary information before their first clinical shift.
* Maintain onboarding checklists and monitor outstanding requirements.
* Support offboarding and transition activities for departing providers.

* Assist providers with navigating administrative requirements related to credentialing, onboarding, compliance training, and hospital access.
* Maintain program records in accordance with organizational policies and applicable regulatory requirements.
* Support audits and compliance reviews as requested.

**Administrative Support**

* Coordinate physician meetings, departmental meetings, interviews, orientations, and special events.
* Prepare correspondence, reports, presentations, spreadsheets, and other program materials.
* Maintain confidential physician, employee, and business information.
* Assist with purchase orders, invoices, expense reimbursement, supplies, and other departmental administrative activities as assigned.
* Participate in process-improvement initiatives designed to improve program efficiency and physician experience.

  

**Minimum Requirements**

**Education:**

* Associate's or bachelor's degree in healthcare administration, business administration, human resources, health services, or a related field.

**Experience:**

* Three or more years of progressively responsible administrative, healthcare operations, physician practice, medical staff, or program coordination experience.
* Experience coordinating multiple priorities, schedules, and stakeholders in a fast-paced environment.

**Preferred:**

* Three to five years of experience within a hospital, medical group, physician practice, or healthcare organization.

* Ability to manage complex physician schedules and frequent schedule changes.

jobs.title: Project Manager, Pre-commercialization
jobs.description:
### **BUILT ON FLAVOR. FUELED BY PEOPLE.**

What's it like to work at Kinder's? Well, there's a lot of snacking and geeking out over what we all cooked over the weekend. Beyond that, there's also plenty of hard work. Because we don't just like flavor, we're obsessed with it.

With over 100 products sold nationwide, we're now a top-five brand in multiple flavor categories at Costco, Walmart, Whole Foods, and more. We're not your typical CPG company. Privately held and founder-led, we like to think of ourselves as a pirate ship in a sea of cruise ships. Our crew is adventurous and fearless. We chart our own course and chase big ideas to make food unforgettable.

As we expand globally and approach $1 billion in revenue, we need more smart-and-scrappy, flavor-obsessed people to come aboard. If you're looking for a place where you can see the real impact of your work... **this is it!** Every day, you'll be part of a journey to add flavor to millions of meals and lives.

### **How You Will Have an Impact at Kinder's****:**

The Pre-Commercialization Project Manager plays a critical role in helping Kinder's bring innovation to life by guiding new product opportunities through the earliest stages of development. You'll help build confidence that great ideas can become great products - ones that meet Kinder's high standards, delight our consumers, and can be successfully brought to market.

Working closely with the Senior Pre-Commercialization Project Manager, you'll guide innovation projects through discovery, feasibility, validation, and development. You'll bring the right people and information together, ask the questions that need to be answered, and connect the dots across functions to help teams make informed decisions and keep projects moving forward.

Pre-Commercialization is an exciting and critical step in bringing Kinder's innovation to life - where we build confidence in whether an opportunity is worth pursuing, whether we can create a product that meets our high standards and consumers' expectations, and whether we have the capabilities to successfully bring it to market. This role requires a balance of structure and agility: applying rigor where it adds value, adapting as we learn, and maintaining a bias toward action.

You'll own portfolio-level PMO analytics across all pre-commercialization projects, translating project data into clear insights that improve visibility, prioritization, resource planning, and decision-making.

You'll partner closely with Culinary, Innovation, R&D, Operations, Supply Chain, Finance, and Commercialization to help turn promising ideas into products we're proud to put the Kinder's name on.

### **What You'll Be Doing**

**Guide Innovation Through Pre-Commercialization**

* Manage a portfolio of innovation projects through discovery, feasibility, validation, and development.

* Bring cross-functional teams together to clarify objectives, answer critical questions, and determine what is needed to move opportunities forward.

* Proactively seek out information, surface gaps, and connect inputs across functions to develop a clear and cohesive picture of each opportunity.

* Maintain momentum by driving actions, decisions, and accountability while adapting as new information and learnings emerge.

**Guide Readiness and Feasibility**

* Guide cross-functional teams in evaluating the relevant feasibility considerations for each opportunity, including culinary, technical, operational, supply chain, financial, and commercial needs.

* Ensure teams have the information needed to determine whether concepts can deliver against Kinder's standards and consumer expectations while being viable to commercialize.

* Identify and clarify key risks, assumptions, dependencies, capabilities, and open questions that need to be addressed.

* Help teams synthesize information and navigate trade-offs to support thoughtful, timely decisions.

**Drive Project Planning and Cross-Functional Alignment**

* Develop and maintain clear project plans in Wrike, including key deliverables, milestones, decisions, risks, and ownership.

* Lead project meetings, feasibility reviews, and cross-functional alignment sessions that drive decisions and action.

* Communicate project status, decisions, risks, and next steps clearly across teams.

* Proactively work through roadblocks and ensure stakeholders understand what's needed to keep projects moving.

* Facilitate effective handoff to Commercialization Project Managers with clear alignment and documentation of key decisions, assumptions, and requirements.

**Own Portfolio Analytics and PMO Reporting**

* Own and maintain PMO analytics across all pre-commercialization projects, providing a consistent and accurate view of portfolio health, stage, timelines, milestones, risks, dependencies, decisions, and resource needs.

* Develop and maintain portfolio dashboards, reports, and key performance indicators in Wrike and related tools to identify trends, bottlenecks, capacity constraints, and opportunities for improvement.

* Analyze project and portfolio data and translate it into actionable insights and recommendations that support leadership decisions, project prioritization, resource allocation, and timely escalation.

* Establish clear data standards and reporting cadences, and partner with project owners to ensure portfolio information is complete, current, and reliable.

**Strengthen How We Work**

* Leverage established Pre-Commercialization tools and frameworks to bring appropriate structure and consistency to project evaluation.

* Identify practical opportunities to improve tools, processes, and ways of working based on project learnings and organizational needs.

* Capture and share learnings that strengthen future innovation projects and cross-functional collaboration.

### **What You Bring to the Table:**

jobs.title: Program Manager, Registration and Aquarium Operations
jobs.description:
**About the California Academy of Sciences**

Founded in 1853, the California Academy of Sciences is a globally renowned, AZA-accredited non-profit scientific and cultural institution located in the heart of San Francisco's Golden Gate Park. Home to a world-class planetarium, aquarium, rainforest, research institute, and natural history museum—all under one living roof—our mission is to regenerate the natural world through science, learning, and collaboration.

Our living collection reflects Earth's vast biodiversity, consisting of nearly 60,000 animals representing over 800 species. Our research collections are the largest west of the Mississippi, spanning nearly 46 million plants, animals, fossils, and cultural artifacts from across the globe and throughout history. Our diverse team includes leading biodiversity scientists, educators, storytellers, designers, and communicators who are passionate about advancing knowledge and catalyzing action through science and storytelling.

Whether you're conducting research behind the scenes or engaging the public on the museum floor, your work will help connect people to the natural world and empower them to protect it.

**About the Opportunity**

  

The Steinhart Aquarium is currently seeking a Registration and Operations Manager to join our team. Reporting to the Curator of Aquarium Operations, this position is split between registration and recordkeeping (approximately 60% of duties) and managing departmental operations (approximately 40% of the role). As the lead registration staff member, you will oversee the Institutional Recordkeeping Program for the Steinhart Aquarium, and ensure that all records are kept up to date and in accordance with the best practices and industry standards set by the Association of Zoos and Aquariums (AZA). Working with minimal oversight and supervision, you will be accountable for managing and maintaining the collection inventory, animal transactions (loans, acquisitions and transfers), births and deaths, transfers between enclosures, behavioral and reproductive notes, and similar program elements. This role ensures that our record-keeping system provides sufficient detail to enhance husbandry, breeding, conservation and medical health advancements to move forward the critical knowledge of species through permanent, retrievable documentation. Operational duties include tracking safety and compliance programs, scheduling meetings and staff training sessions, and coordinating the recruiting and onboarding of departmental volunteers. Work schedule may include weekends, evenings and holidays.

**Organizational Culture**

  

When you join the California Academy of Sciences, you become part of a mission-driven community that values curiosity, collaboration, and innovation, and celebrates its accomplishments together. Staff share a commitment to executing a new strategic plan that will strengthen the organization's financial foundations, cultivate a vibrant internal culture, and foster smart growth to secure the Academy's future.

We hope you are inspired by what we do and are motivated to contribute to our mission. The Academy is looking for candidates who do great work, and we know they may come from a number of different backgrounds and experiences. We encourage you to apply even if you do not believe you meet every qualification for the position.

This position is based in San Francisco, California. The specific onsite/hybrid schedule for this position is listed below.

**This position is part of a bargaining unit represented by Cal Academy Workers United, and will be subject to the terms and conditions of that contract.**

**About the Steinhart Aquarium Team**

Steinhart Aquarium is one of the most biologically diverse and interactive aquariums on Earth. Home to more than 60,000 live plants and animals, representing more than 1,000 unique species, it offers guests an unprecedented view of underwater and terrestrial habitats.

**Key Responsibilities**

  

A critical aspect of this position is maintaining the Steinhart Aquarium Institutional Recordkeeping Program, and assisting departmental managers in maintaining all protocols, procedures, recordkeeping and standards. Responsibilities related to managing the Steinhart Aquarium's animal database, digital workflow, and federal and state permits are expected to account for approximately 60% of the role. These include:

* Animal Records Database – independently responsible for ensuring the accuracy and integrity of our animal collections data in the ZIMS global database, tracking the daily ins and outs of the collection through departmental systems such as PI Reports and Mortality Reports. Trains and onboards all new staff to our recordkeeping systems, policies, and standards, and activates/deactivates staff ZIMS accounts. Ensures that all records are kept up to date and in accordance with the best practices and industry standards set by the Association of Zoos and Aquariums (AZA).
* Permits – independently responsible for ensuring that all departmental state and federal permits are accurate, up to date, and renewed on schedule, and that all annual reporting requirements are completed on schedule.
* Formstack – independently monitors, maintains, and updates our digital workflow and permissions systems in the Formstack software platform.
* Google Suite – independently monitors, maintains, and updates our Google sites page, team drives, and Google email groups.
* Graphics – processes new graphic ID requests for the Steinhart Aquarium and Rainforest exhibits. Collaborates with the Steinhart biologists, IBSS scientists, and Experience Studio to create and produce both digital and printed graphics.

Duties related to departmental operations and administration are expected to account for approximately 40% of the role. These include:

* Safety & Compliance – supports the Curator of Aquarium Operations to ensure that we are operating within all safety and regulatory guidelines

**Job Title: Community Health Worker**

**About JFS of Silicon Valley (JFSSV):**

Jewish Family Services of Silicon Valley envisions a world where each person achieves self-sufficiency, stability, well-being, and purpose. JFS SV is an inclusive nonprofit social services organization providing comprehensive support services to individuals and families facing life challenges. We engage community partners and collectively we make a positive impact on the lives of those we serve. As an inclusive organization, our biggest strengths are the unwavering support we provide to all employees and the celebration of diversity amongst all communities.

**Job Summary:**

Under the supervision of a Care Manager, the Community Health Worker provides essential administrative, logistical, and direct-support assistance to facilitate the delivery of care management services to CALAIM authorized members. The CHW supports the care management team in coordinating community-based services, conducting outreach, processing referrals, and ensuring clients receive timely and dignified access to the programs and resources they need. This role requires compassion, attention to detail, strong organizational skills, and the ability to work effectively with a diverse population.

**Key Responsibilities:**

Member Outreach & Engagement: Contacting members who may need care coordination, following up on gaps in care, and helping hard-to-reach populations engage with services. Monitor client well-being through regular phone or in-person check-ins and report changes in status to the supervising Care Manager.

Care Coordination Support: Working alongside care managers and nurses to support members with chronic conditions, complex needs, or social determinants of health (SDOH) barriers. Assist Care Managers in implementing individualized care plans for clients. Accompany Care Managers on home visits and community assessments as needed; may conduct follow-up visits independently under supervision.

Navigation & Resource Linkage: Connecting members to community resources such as food assistance, housing, transportation, and behavioral health services. Schedule and coordinate client appointments, home visits, and service provider contacts. Provide clients and caregivers with information about available community resources, benefits programs, and county services. Coordinate linkage to services including IHSS, Meals on Wheels, transportation, adult day programs, mental health services, housing support, and other community-based programs.

Health Education: Providing culturally and linguistically appropriate health education to members and their families.

Administrative Support: Documenting outreach attempts, updating member records, and tracking referrals in the care management system. Assist clients in completing applications for public benefits, including Medi-Cal, CalFresh, Medicare Savings Programs, and other entitlements.

Cultural Bridging: Serving as a liaison between the health plan, providers, and the community, particularly for underserved or non-English-speaking populations.

**Qualifications:**

Education:

* High school diploma or GED, prior experience in community social services, health education and care coordination.

Experience:

* Minimum 1-2 years of experience in a social services, health care, or community-based organization setting.
* Experience working with adults.
* Experience working with underserved, low income or culturally diverse populations, lived experience

Skills and Competencies

* Knowledge of community resources, social service programs, and public benefits available to adults in Santa Clara County.
* Ability to communicate clearly and empathetically with clients, families, and service providers from diverse backgrounds.
* Strong organizational skills with the ability to manage multiple cases and deadlines simultaneously.
* Proficiency in Microsoft Office (Word, Excel, Outlook) and ability to learn case management software.
* Ability to maintain confidentiality and adhere to HIPAA and other privacy regulations.
* Cultural competency and sensitivity
* Ability to navigate community resources and social services
* Basic computer and documentation skills for entering data and tracking outreach
* Motivational interviewing or health coaching skills are a plus
* Commitment to integrating JFS SV's core values into all aspects of work: Respect and Dignity for All, Welcoming the Stranger, Repairing the World
* Bilingual proficiency in Russian, Spanish, Vietnamese, Mandarin, Cantonese, or other language(s) reflecting the county's population is highly desirable.

jobs.title: Senior E-Commerce & Web Operations Manager
jobs.description:
At Ouster, we build sensors and tools for engineers, roboticists, and researchers, so they can make the world safer and more efficient. We've transformed LIDAR from an analog device with thousands of components to an elegant digital device powered by one chip-scale laser array and one CMOS sensor. The result is a full range of high-resolution LIDAR sensors that deliver superior imaging at a dramatically lower price. Our advanced sensor hardware and vision algorithms are used in autonomous cars, drones and many other applications. If you’re motivated by solving big problems, we’re hiring key roles across the company and need your help!  
  
**Role Overview**

We are seeking an execution-focused Senior E-Commerce & Web Operations Manager to co-own the delivery of our web store platform and manage our corporate digital presence as we grow our direct online channel.

In this role, you will be the commercial and operational engine behind our direct online sales channel. You will adopt and scale the proven webstore playbook established by our Stereolabs team, drive self-service adoption for our REV8 sensors and accessories, and rigorously manage our corporate website (Ouster.com) and agency partners to ensure high efficiency, minimal scope creep, and fast execution. Your work will enable Ouster to reach and support customers around the world we previously couldn't serve.

This is an individual contributor role, partnering closely with cross-functional teams, our Stereolabs team in Paris, and external agency and implementation partners.

**Responsibilities**

**Webstore Ownership & GTM Execution**

* Co-Own Project Delivery: Partner with cross-functional teams (Product Strategy, Sales, IT, Legal, Audit, Finance, and Support) to help deliver our webstore launch in a phased approach, then drive the store's day-to-day operations after go-live.
* Playbook Execution: Adopt and adapt the operational e-commerce workflow from our Stereolabs team (Paris) using Shopify and our implementation partner.
* Catalog Management: Own SKU onboarding, implementation of pricing and promotions (in partnership with sales and product strategy), bundles, datasheets, and customer-facing descriptions for Ouster REV8 sensors, cables, and components. This includes managing ongoing changes to SKUs, pricing, and product content as applicable.
* Revenue & Self-Service Growth: Build campaigns and conversion flows to route low-touch, long-tail accounts through self-service e-commerce.
* Performance Reporting: Define and report on webstore KPIs (traffic, conversion, order volume, self-serve revenue, quote deflection) and use them to prioritize improvements.

**Corporate Web Operations & Agency Management (Ouster.com)**

* Website Unification: Lead the consolidation of Stereolabs.com into Ouster.com to streamline our global digital footprint and domain architecture. This includes content migration, redirect mapping, and preservation of search rankings and inbound traffic.
* Agency & Vendor Management: Directly manage our external web agency partners with strict oversight on scope, deliverables, speed, and budget. Shift routine work in-house and right-size the agency engagement over time.
* In-House CMS Management: Use Sanity CMS to swiftly build and launch new landing pages, product pages, and digital assets internally without relying heavily on agency development.

**Qualifications & Requirements**

* Experience: 5+ years owning e-commerce and/or web operations within B2B Hardware, B2C Consumer Tech, B2B Software, Industrial Tech, Marketplaces, or Semiconductor sectors.
* E-Commerce Stack: Hands-on admin experience with Shopify / Shopify Plus, product information architecture, catalog management, and checkout flows.
* Modern CMS & Web Stack: Proven experience with Sanity (or other headless CMS platforms) and managing web design/build projects.
* Site Migrations: Has led at least one domain consolidation or site migration with SEO preserved.
* Agency Management: Demonstrated track record of holding creative and technical agencies accountable to strict budgets, SOWs, and delivery timelines, including cutting agency spend or bringing work in-house.
* Mindset: Pragmatic operator who prioritizes execution and speed-to-market over perfection or unnecessary redesigns.
* Collaboration: Comfortable working across time zones with teams in the US and France.

  
The base pay will be dependent on your skills, work experience, location, and qualifications. This role may also be eligible for equity & benefits. ($130,000 - $170,000)

jobs.title: Staff Product Operations Manager
jobs.description:
**Why Socure?**
---------------

Socure is building the identity trust infrastructure for the digital economy — verifying 100% of good identities in real time and stopping fraud before it starts. The mission is big, the problems are complex, and the impact is felt by businesses, governments, and millions of people every day.

We hire people who want that level of responsibility. People who move fast, think critically, act like owners, and care deeply about solving customer problems with precision. If you want predictability or narrow scope, this won’t be your place. If you want to help build the future of identity with a team that holds a high bar for itself — keep reading.

**About the Role**
------------------

Product Operations exists to give product teams the systems, data, and processes they need to plan, prioritize, and deliver well — the same way Sales Ops supports Sales or DevOps supports Engineering. This role sits at the center of that discipline, contributing to three core areas: the **reporting and analytics** that give everyone visibility into what's happening, the **process** that makes planning and delivery repeatable instead of reinvented pod by pod, and the ongoing work of keeping **strategy and execution connected** as priorities shift.

We run Product Operations as a **hybrid centralized/embedded model**: some Product Ops work sits centrally and serves every product team consistently, while other Product Ops work sits embedded inside individual product lines, close to their day-to-day priorities. This role sits in the centralized hub — you're the shared systems, process, and reporting engine that every embedded product manager and product ops partner relies on, rather than being dedicated to any single product line.

We're a small team, so this role is intentionally broad. At larger companies, "owns the tools," "owns the reporting," and "owns the process" are sometimes split into two or three separate roles. Here, one person does all of it, with the flexibility to shift emphasis as priorities and team size change over time.

**What You'll Do**
------------------

### **Support reporting & analytics for the Product Org**

* Build and maintain the dashboards and reports that give leadership and embedded product teams a reliable view of roadmap status, delivery progress, and portfolio health.
* Define and track core product operations metrics (e.g., cycle time, roadmap adherence, planning hygiene, tool adoption).
* Centralize and facilitate Product Performance metrics definition, telemetry builds, and availability to central data and BI teams, and coordinate dashboard and reporting builds with the central Business Intelligence team to enable deeper insights and faster decision making for the Product Team.
* Partner with Finance, Sales/RevOps, and Engineering to bring commercial and delivery data (e.g., CRM/ARR data) into product prioritization and reporting.
* Support recurring reporting cadences — business reviews, quarterly/annual planning, board updates — with clean, trusted data.
* Monitor data quality and drive hygiene standards across the systems that feed reporting.

### **Drive process, efficiency & team enablement**

* Design and document repeatable processes for planning, prioritization, intake, and roadmap reviews — so teams have a consistent way of working instead of reinventing it pod by pod.
* Identify friction points and manual, duplicative work in the product development lifecycle, and fix them — through better process, automation, or tooling.
* Build templates, playbooks, and checklists (e.g., for feature intake, roadmap reviews, launch readiness) that save product managers time and reduce administrative burden.
* Act as the go-to resource for product managers and embedded product ops partners on how to use shared tools and processes effectively — training, office hours, documentation.
* Facilitate cross-functional handoffs between Product, Engineering, Design, and GTM so work moves smoothly instead of stalling on a handoff.
* Continuously look for opportunities to standardize process across pods while leaving room for the flexibility each team actually needs.

### **Keep strategy and execution aligned**

* Partner with product leadership to translate high-level strategy and company priorities into a concrete, trackable roadmap and planning cadence.
* Run the rhythm of planning — quarterly/annual planning cycles, roadmap reviews, and business reviews — that keeps execution connected to strategy as priorities shift.
* Monitor progress against strategic priorities and flag early when day-to-day execution is drifting from what leadership actually intended.
* Support trade-off and prioritization conversations when competing asks conflict with stated strategic priorities, so decisions get made deliberately rather than by default.
* Make sure work happening inside individual pods visibly ladders up to company-level strategic themes, not just local priorities.
* Close the loop after major planning moments — make sure decisions made in a review actually get reflected in the systems everyone works from day to day.

**What Success Looks Like**
---------------------------

* Product teams and Leadership trust the systems and data they're working from.
* Leadership can get a reliable answer about roadmap and delivery status without a scramble.
* Tooling stays consistent and well-governed instead of fragmenting pod by pod.
* Planning cycles run on schedule, supported by clean data rather than last-minute reconciliation.
* Teams spend less time on manual coordination and administrative busywork, and more time making strategic decisions.
* Roadmap execution visibly ladders up to strategic priorities — and when it drifts, that gets caught and surfaced early, not discovered at quarter-end.
* Cross-functional handoffs happen through defined, repeatable processes instead of ad hoc effort every time.
* System and reporting knowledge is documented and shared, not held by one

Our SF HQ at 165 Page St is an office, a studio and an event venue. In one week we can host a panel and a DJ night with projection mapping, take partner visits and keep a full team working. You'll run the building, its vendors, our events and the community around them, and you'll work as EA to one of our founders.

Expect to spend around 40% of your time on office and facilities: letting vendors in, testing their fixes, and receiving and installing deliveries. Another 30% goes to events and community, where you run our event series and grow the community that comes out of it. The last 30% is vendor and executive coordination. You track each open item in writing until you close it. You'll do most of this work on site at our SF HQ.

**What you'll own**
-------------------

**1. Property management and maintenance (daily)**

* Act as our single point of contact with the landlord and property manager. File maintenance requests through their portal, follow up on walkthroughs and chase each ticket until it closes.
* Be on site when contractors do the work. Show the plumber the problem, test the shower after the fix, check the garage door and confirm the keycards work.
* Follow the escalation rules: send routine requests by email or portal, and save texts to the property manager for emergencies.

**2. Vendors and building systems (daily)**

* Own the building vendors end to end: security and alarm monitoring, fire and smoke detector service, keycard and access control, internet, trash and recycling, plumbing, cleaning and janitorial, laundry, catering and handyman work.
* Get quotes, compare them, book the work, let techs in, check the result and reconcile the invoice.
* Handle light office IT and access yourself. You'll set up and maintain the Wi-Fi gear, manage keycards and the door access system, and take cameras and smart locks from install to working.
* Learn the building systems cold (alarm silence and reset, access readers, cameras and the panel) so you can handle a tripped detector at 9pm.
* Set the weekly cadence for cleaning, laundry, restocking and trash days so the team walks into a ready office each morning.

**3. Purchasing and receiving (several times a week)**

* Run the office purchase list. Confirm items, quantities and deadlines, check what we've already ordered, and place orders across Amazon, Home Depot, Costco, Instacart and local stores.
* Receive packages, chase missed or returned deliveries with the carrier, and handle returns.
* Install mounts, AV, lighting, furniture and signage, or bring in someone who can.

**4. Event operations (weekly, heavy in event weeks)**

* Run event operations for anything from a 30-person dinner to a 500+ RSVP party: catering, licensed bartenders and drink tickets, DJ and AV, furniture, check-in and cleanup.
* Own event safety and compliance. You'll manage haze and smoke rules in a building with an interconnected fire alarm, QR waivers and 21+ ID checks at the door, security staff, roped-off areas, capacity and event insurance.
* Run crowd control and stage management for intense DJ nights: entry flow and capacity counts, the stage and DJ booth perimeter, crowd surges near the front, security staff placement and a tight run-of-show for changeovers.
* Scout and book outside venues when an event outgrows our space. Keep a vendor list with quotes on file so you can plan each event faster and for less money.

**5. Community, offline and online (weekly)**

* Help run our offline community. You'll host a steady series of events and turn first-time guests into regulars, and regulars into core members.
* Track who comes, who comes back and who brings friends. Follow up with the good ones so they return after their first night.
* Move people from our events into our online community (group chats, Discord or Slack, and newsletters), and keep that space active between events.
* After each event, report RSVPs, show rate, new members and repeat attendees.

**6. Facilities and security policy (as needed)**

* Set and enforce building rules for package handling, door access and guests, plus a stopgap plan for the period before cameras and alarms go live.

**7. EA and executive operations for one of our founders (constant)**

* Turn the founder's quick notes and voice memos into tracked tasks with owners and dates.
* Handle day-to-day errands, purchases, scheduling, logistics and vendor calls so the founder can spend their time on the company.
* Write clear vendor and landlord emails in English, run follow-up checks, and flag a risk as soon as you see it.
* Turn recurring problems into checklists, runbooks, vendor rosters and trackers so you solve each problem once.

**Who you are**
---------------

* You have several years running office, facilities, hospitality or venue operations at a startup, hotel, venue or event space, and you've run a building day to day.
* You have a track record of events you ran, with results you can point to. A recurring series counts for more than one-offs.
* You've built an offline community. Across many events, you turned first-time guests into regulars and grew a core group that keeps showing up.
* You've run an online community, moved people into it from in-person events and kept it active.
* You have a network to call on. If we need catering for 80 on Thursday, a deep clean after a party, a laundry service or a fire-alarm tech, you know who to call or how to find them fast.
* You have hands-on crowd control and stage management experience from packed, intense events: DJ nights, club nights or concerts.
* You're comfortable with building systems and event safety: alarms, access control, capacity, bar service and waivers.

jobs.description:
**About Plasmidsaurus**

Plasmidsaurus is on a mission to accelerate new cures and promote a healthier planet by unlocking a new level of productivity for scientists. Our sequencing services are used daily by thousands of innovators, including Nobel laureates, Fortune 100 pharma, and over 70,000 scientists.

We began by revolutionizing plasmid sequencing, making it exponentially cheaper and faster, with innovative sequencing technologies and a global network of laboratories that turn samples into answers in hours, not weeks.

Now we are expanding that same disruptive model across all of genomics. With the launch of our new RNA-seq service, we are taking a bold step toward our vision to sequence everything, providing scientists everywhere with faster, simpler, and more affordable access to the data that powers discovery.

Every team member at Plasmidsaurus plays a crucial role in driving the future of biotech research. Together, we are building the world’s most efficient sequencing engine that operates overnight, scales globally, and helps scientists make breakthroughs faster than ever before.

**Role Overview**
=================

Plasmidsaurus is looking for a Senior Project Manager to build a project management function to help us execute more high-impact, cross-functional work, faster.

You’ll turn our existing patchwork of project and task management processes into an effective, practical system for managing new product development and product improvement projects from inception through launch, and monitoring overall health and velocity our project portfolio.

This is a builder role. You won’t be stepping into an established PMO or simply managing a portfolio of existing project plans. You’ll have the opportunity to establish how project management works at Plasmidsaurus, build the system that help us prioritize our most important work, and you’ll be the driving force behind high impact projects across the company.

**What You'll Do**
==================

### **Build the Project Management System**

* Operationalize our existing product development and product commercialization processes into a standardized project management system that teams actually use.
* Establish practical standards for project planning, milestones, ownership, dependencies, risks, decisions, resources, and reporting.
* Integrate project management with the tools teams already use, including Notion, Linear, and Slack.
* Train and support project and functional leads in using the system effectively.
* Continuously improve the system based on what works, what doesn’t, and what teams need as we scale.

### **Drive Strategic Projects**

* Lead complex, cross-functional product development and product improvement projects from inception through launch.
* Establish clear plans, owners, milestones, dependencies, and committed dates.
* Keep teams aligned and accountable, identifying risks, blockers and constraints early and driving them toward resolution.
* Create the coordination and visibility needed to increase project velocity and improve performance against launch commitments.

### **Create Portfolio Visibility**

* Build a clear portfolio view of project health, priorities, resources, dependencies, and constraints that allows teams to make better decisions about what work gets done, when, and with what resources
* Help teams and leadership understand how new projects and changing priorities affect work already in flight.
* Improve our ability to forecast timelines, understand capacity, and make informed decisions about what we take on.
* Use project and portfolio data to identify opportunities to increase the amount of work we can successfully execute.

**What Success Looks Like in Your First 90 Days**
=================================================

You’ve built a project management system that teams across Product, Engineering, R&D, Production, Operations and Marketing use to plan and execute their work.

You’ve taken an active role in our highest-priority cross-functional projects, creating clearer ownership, timelines, dependencies, decisions, and visibility into blockers.

Leadership has a clearer view of the project portfolio and the information needed to make better decisions about priorities, resources, capacity, and new work.

**Who You Are**
===============

* **A builder.** You create systems that work in practice, test them, and improve them rather than defaulting to process for process’s sake.
* **A systems thinker.** You understand how people, processes, resources, and decisions interact and optimize for the whole rather than one piece.
* **A leader.** You can create alignment and accountability across teams without relying on authority and can mentor other project leaders on best practices and how to use the system you build.
* **An efficient problem solver.** You identify what matters most while avoiding lower priority distractions, get to the root of ambiguous problems, evaluate tradeoffs, and find practical ways forward even when information or resources are limited.
* **A clear communicator.** You turn complexity into information people can understand and use to make decisions.
* **Technically fluent.** You understand technical and scientific work well enough to identify dependencies, ask useful questions, and work credibly with R&D and Engineering teams.
* **Adept with technology.** You use AI, automation, integrations, and other tools to simplify workflows, connect systems, and reduce project-management overhead.

**Your Background**
===================

* Bachelor's degree or equivalent experience required.
* PMP preferred. Other relevant project management training or certification considered.

jobs.description:
**Build at the Highest level | FORMA Construction**

**Come build the projects you want to be known for.**

FORMA was founded with a clear Mission: to be **the most respected partner for highly complex and detailed residential projects.**

You will lead sophisticated custom residential projects involving exceptional architecture, demanding details, discerning clients, and some of the best architects, designers, and craftspeople in the industry.

We are looking for experienced construction leaders who love the challenge of complicated projects, take pride in being exceptionally prepared, want real responsibility, and are motivated by working alongside other highly capable people.

If you are competitive about your craft, if you like being trusted with difficult things, and if being surrounded by excellent people makes you want to raise your own game, **you should keep reading.**

FORMA has spent years building some of California's most distinctive residences.

Our current portfolio includes projects with some of the most respected architecture and design firms in the industry, including **Feldman Architecture, Butler Armsden Architects, Studio Vara, Marmol Radziner, Ingrao Design, EYRC Architects and KOVAC Architecture.**

Our work ranges from complex structural transformations in San Francisco to major ground-up residences throughout the Bay Area—and now into Southern California.

**OUR CULTURE: A TEAM, NOT A FAMILY**

We take culture seriously, so we'll be clear about ours.

**FORMA is a team. We are not a family.**

A great team is built around a shared objective and for us, that is winning championships by turning clients into advocates. To win, we only hire the best, most capable people, because every position matters!

But high standards do **not** mean a cutthroat environment. Great teams invest in their players.

And like a great team, We coach. We practice. We teach. We leverage experience and provide tools and resources. We believe that when you give great people, great tools and training, you allow talented people opportunities to stretch themselves to become even better.

If that philosophy energizes you rather than intimidates you, you will probably understand FORMA.

**HOW WE OPERATE -** Four ideas shape how we work.

* **OWNERSHIP:** We take personal responsibility for outcomes—solving problems, owning the details, and driving results
* **URGENCY:** We act with clarity, purpose, and discipline to propel projects forward without delay or compromise.
* **COMMUNICATION:** We empower every stake holder with context and to make confident decisions through timely, thoughtful, and proactive communication.
* **CRAFT:** We commit to artistry, precision, and innovation, ensuring meticulous execution of complex, finely crafted homes.

**WHAT YOU WILL OWN**

The Project Manager is responsible for the **business leadership of the project,** from preconstruction and buyout through construction and closeout.

You will work in close partnership with the Superintendent and Assistant Project Manager, but you are ultimately expected to maintain command of the project's financial, contractual, scheduling and client-facing information.

That includes:

**Financial leadership**

* Own the project budget, cost tracking, forecasting, committed costs, cost coding and cash-flow projections.
* Manage subcontractor buyout and purchasing.
* Review and approve invoices.
* Understand where the project is financially today and, more importantly, where it is going.
* Identify exposure early rather than explaining overruns later.
* Lead change management from early ROM pricing through client approval, contract change orders and final billing.

**Planning and schedule**

* Develop and maintain a meaningful CPM project schedule in collaboration with the Superintendent.
* Understand critical path, procurement, submittals, RFIs and design decisions and how each affects the schedule.
* Look weeks and months ahead—not just at what needs to happen tomorrow.
* Recognize potential delays early and create a plan to address them.

**Project leadership**

* Maintain command of the project.
* Run effective OAC meetings.
* Know the budget.
* Know the schedule.
* Know the outstanding design issues.
* Know the decisions that need to be made.
* Know who owes what to whom and when.
* Your client, architect, Superintendent and internal team should leave meetings with greater clarity because you were in the room.

**Client and design-team partnership**

* Serve as a primary point of contact for sophisticated clients and their representatives.
* Communicate clearly about budget, schedule, design decisions, risks and opportunities.
* Develop productive relationships with architects, interior designers, consultants and owner's representatives.
* Handle difficult conversations early, professionally and directly.
* Protect the relationship without avoiding the issue.

**Contract and risk management**

* Understand the prime contract and your subcontract agreements.
* Write thorough scopes.
* Manage RFIs, submittals, bulletins, SKs and other project documentation.
* Recognize contractual and project risk early and take action to protect the client, the project and FORMA.

**Team development**

* Manage and develop your Assistant Project Manager.
* Partner closely with the Superintendent rather than operating in a separate silo.
* Teach what you know.
* Raise the level of the people around you.

**YOU MAY LOVE WORKING HERE IF...**

* You enjoy being surrounded by highly capable people.
* You want real responsibility.
* You like difficult projects.
* You appreciate direct feedback.
* You enjoy teaching others and learning from people who are exceptional at what they do.
* You want access to strong systems, technology and resources rather than spending your career fighting organizational dysfunction.
* You care about architecture and craftsmanship but also understand that great construction is a business.

jobs.description:
**About the Role**
  
  
We are looking for an L5 Program Manager to join Delivery Product Insights & Rollouts and own product and rollout readiness across a major Uber Delivery Persona. This role sits at the intersection of Product, Tech, CX, Operations and Data, and is accountable for turning complex launch information into a clear, trusted readiness view and recommendation.
  
  
The role will likely own a Persona lane and may flex across Personas as business priorities evolve. As the broader xLOB operating model develops, the role may also contribute to Quality and continuous experience improvement.
  
  
This role requires end-to-end ownership. The right person can understand the product and technical system deeply enough to identify what can impact the customer or support experience, evaluate the evidence, challenge assumptions, drive cross-functional decisions, and hold the organization to a clear readiness bar.
  
  
**What You'll Do**

* Own end-to-end readiness for material product and technology rollouts within an assigned Persona, from early planning through launch, scale and post-launch monitoring

* Represent the Persona in Product and Tech planning and use launch / post-launch evidence to identify experience opportunities, improve quality, and strengthen the readiness model over time
* + Partner with central capabilities to apply common standards while preserving the Persona context required for strong readiness and experience decisions.

jobs.title: Patient Services Coordinator
jobs.description:
Baywell Psychiatry Group is a growing physician-owned practice of psychiatrists and psychotherapists serving children, adults, and seniors across the SF Bay Area. We offer psychiatric consultations, psychotherapy, and medication management. We take pride in providing high-quality mental health care and providing access to a diverse range of people. You will be the first point of contact for people seeking mental health help and can make a lot of difference for community access.

As a small, close-knit team, we rely on every member to show up fully, pitch in wherever needed, and care as much about the details as we do. If you’re someone who thrives in a dynamic environment, takes initiative, and finds purpose in supporting others, this role is for you.

We’re looking for a motivated, compassionate Patient Services Coordinator to join our San Francisco and San Mateo offices. This is a great opportunity for anyone passionate about mental health or pursuing a future in healthcare as you’ll gain real, hands-on experience in a fast-paced clinical setting.

**This is an in-person and full-time position based in our San Francisco or San Mateo office.**

**What You’ll Do**

This role is phone and email heavy. You’ll be the voice of Baywell, often the first person a patient speaks with, sometimes during emotionally difficult moments in their lives. We’re looking for someone who can bring warmth and calm to every interaction without absorbing the emotional weight of those conversations.

Because we’re a small business, no two days look exactly alike. You’ll be expected to jump in on whatever the team needs, big tasks or small, and shift priorities quickly when the situation calls for it. Specific responsibilities include:

* Serving as the primary point of contact for patients by phone - answering calls, scheduling appointments, and creating a warm, professional experience
* Coordinating communication between patients, physicians, and the administrative team via phone, email, and fax
* Guiding new patients through the intake process, educating them about their health insurance benefits, and welcoming them to the office
* Maintaining and managing physician and therapist schedules with accuracy and flexibility ensuring doctor calendars are full
* Processing prescription refills and prior authorization requests
* Handling day-to-day administrative tasks including insurance coordination, record-keeping, and faxes
* Jumping in to support teammates and cover tasks outside your usual scope when needed - we have a small team and everyone contributes
* Adapting quickly as priorities shift throughout the day, staying organized and composed under pressure
* Supporting our clinical team so they can focus on delivering exceptional patient care

**What We’re Looking For**

The right candidate brings more than administrative skills – they bring emotional intelligence, flexibility, and a commitment to showing up for their team and their patients.

* Exceptional verbal and written communication skills, especially over the phone – you’ll be warm, clear, and professional even when a caller is distressed or frustrated
* A small-business mindset – you’re comfortable with ambiguity, willing to take on any task that comes your way, and don’t wait to be asked twice
* Emotional resilience – you’ll be able to be present with patients dealing with difficult situations without taking on their emotional distress or solving their problem
* Strong adaptability – you can shift gears gracefully when priorities change throughout the day
* Excellent attention to detail and the ability to follow requests and projects all the way to the end
* A dependable, consistent work ethic and a professional demeanor
* Ability to work both independently and as a close collaborator on a small team
* Genuine sensitivity to mental health issues and a firm commitment to patient confidentiality
* A bachelor’s degree is preferred (coursework or interest in psychology, pre-med, business, or a related field is a strong plus)
* Experience in a medical office or small business setting is a plus
* Proficiency with computers and Google Workspace; familiarity with medical practice management software is helpful

This role is especially well-suited for candidates with clinical aspirations – the experience you gain here is directly applicable to a career in healthcare.

**Compensation & Benefits**

Salary: $25–$27 per hour, depending on experience

* Health, dental, and vision insurance
* 401(k) with matching
* Life insurance
* Flexible spending account
* Paid time off
* Mentorship and education opportunities from our physician and senior admin team members

Schedule: Monday–Friday, 8-hour shifts in-person in our San Francisco or our San Mateo office. We are looking for someone who can take over the 8am-4:30pm opening shift in San Francisco.

**To Apply**

Please submit the following for immediate consideration:

* A cover letter telling us why this role interests you and what you’d bring to our team
* Your resume
* Two or more professional references

We’re looking for a long-term team member and value candidates who demonstrate stability, focus, and interest in mental health care. We warmly welcome applicants who are newer to the workforce but eager to grow.

*Baywell Psychiatry Group is an equal opportunity employer. We value diversity and do not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, color, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, or disability status.*

Pay: $25.00 - $27.00 per hour

Benefits:

* 401(k) matching
* Dental insurance
* Flexible spending account
* Health insurance
* Life insurance
* Paid time off
* Vision insurance

People with a criminal record are encouraged to apply

Santa Clara County partners with Sourcewise to provide Public Authority Services for In-Home Supportive Services (IHSS).

The Public Authority Registry assists IHSS consumers needing help finding an independent care provider (IP) by maintaining a database of experienced IPs and utilizing technology to provide individualized lists of qualified IPs who a consumer can interview and hire.

Care Coaching is an enhanced service of the Registry, which focuses on assisting consumers who experience significant challenges with their employer responsibilities, including interviewing, hiring, training, and supervising their IPs. These consumers may be paired with a Care Coordinator, who helps them navigate these employer responsibilities.

REQUIREMENTS:

* BSW or equivalent
* Ability to pass DOJ background check requirements in accordance with local laws
* Ability to communicate via telephone and in person, deal tactfully and courteously with the public and agency personnel
* Strong organizational skills, self-starter, exercise independent judgment, problem solve
* Comfortable speaking to small groups in a training setting
* Ability to identify and assess IHSS consumers’ ability to handle the employer responsibilities inherent in the consumer directed mode of service
* Ability to conduct thorough home visits and travel to all areas within Santa Clara County
* Ability to conduct thorough phone interviews
* Ability to provide excellent written documentation
* Experience maintaining case notes and/or keeping accurate detailed records
* Basic knowledge of routine office procedures
* Proficient using a computer in MS word, MS Windows environment
* Interest in working with elderly and disabled individuals
* Bilingual (Spanish/English or Chinese/English preferred)

DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES:  
The duties below are representative of the range of responsibilities expected of the Care Coordinator but are not intended to be all-inclusive:

* Become knowledgeable about Public Authority programs sufficient to answer basic questions regarding: The Registry, training classes, benefits, enrollment, etc.

jobs.title: People Operations Coordinator
jobs.description:
**Own Your Intelligence**
-------------------------

Prime Intellect is building the open superintelligence stack: the infrastructure frontier AI labs build internally, made available to every ambitious AI team.

Our platform, Lab, unifies compute, environments, evaluations, secure sandboxes, high-performance training, and deployment into one full-stack system for post-training at frontier scale - from SFT and RL to tool use, agent workflows, and continuously improving production models. We are building open frontier AI: open-source models trained end to end for long-horizon tasks like autonomous research, and the full-stack platform our own research team uses to build them. The next generation of AI companies, enterprises, and research teams do not just need more GPUs. They need the ability to turn their own workflows, tools, data, and feedback loops into superintelligence they own.

Prime Intellect has raised $150M in total funding from Founders Fund, Radical Ventures, NVIDIA, and exceptional AI, infrastructure, and enterprise operators — including Andrej Karpathy, Dwarkesh Patel, and leaders and founders from Ramp, Perplexity, Harvey, Mercor, Zapier, Datadog, Cognition, OpenAI, Thinking Machines, Together AI, SemiAnalysis, LangChain, Browserbase, Cloudflare, Sierra, Databricks, Airbnb, OpenRouter, Standard Intelligence, Fleet, Core Auto, and more. We are looking for people who want to build at the intersection of frontier research, real infrastructure, and go-to-market for a category that does not fully exist yet.

**Your Role**
-------------

We are a team of about 60, split between our San Francisco office and remote staff, and we are hiring quickly. Every researcher, engineer, and operator who joins us has a first day, a first week, and a first impression of how seriously we take the people who build here. Right now, that experience depends on a lot of people doing a lot of small things right. This role makes it a system.

You will own the employee lifecycle from the moment a candidate is scheduled for an interview through a new hire's first weeks. You will design every new hire's first day, run onboarding end to end, coordinate recruiting logistics across multiple open searches, and help bring the team together in person. You will also be the person who looks at how this function works and makes it faster, more reliable, and more personal — including where AI tools and automation can take the repetitive parts off your plate so you can spend your time on the parts that only a person can do.

This is an in-person role based in our San Francisco office, reporting to our Executive Business Partner and working closely with the Head of Talent, hiring managers, IT, and finance.

**Responsibilities**
--------------------

**Onboarding & Employee Experience**

* Design the first-day schedule and experience for every new hire so they feel welcomed and productive from day one, with a white-glove approach for executive hires
* Set up desks and equipment before day one: laptop, monitor, welcome kit in place; coordinate provisioning, accounts, and tool access with IT
* Coordinate finance onboarding — payroll, benefits enrollment, expense tools, company card — and office access: door access, building entry, and meal program
* Complete required onboarding steps accurately and on time: background checks, I-9 verification, employee records, and HRIS setup
* Identify immigration and visa needs early, route them to the right people, and track them to resolution
* Maintain and continuously improve the onboarding system so every hire gets a consistent, well-run first week
* Support offboarding: recover equipment and remove access

**Recruiting Coordination**

* Own interview scheduling across multiple open roles so every candidate and interviewer shows up informed, prepared, and on time
* Book travel and host candidates for onsite interviews and work trials, creating a warm, human candidate experience
* Keep candidates and hiring teams informed throughout the process with timely, clear communication
* Maintain Ashby as the single source of truth: stage updates, candidate notes, and pipeline hygiene
* Own scheduling timelines and SLAs, surface risks early, and keep recruiters and hiring managers in the loop

**Systems, Culture & Team Operations**

* Find smarter, faster ways to run this function, including automating repetitive work with AI tools
* Track open hiring and onboarding tasks and follow through on every commitment
* Contribute to an in-person culture that builds connection across in-office and remote teams
* Help plan and run team onsites and offsites, including attendee logistics and travel
* Take on recruiting operations and sourcing projects as the function grows

**What Success Looks Like**
---------------------------

* New hires feel expected and cared for. Before day one, they know where to go, what to expect, and who to ask for help.
* Laptops arrive on time, accounts work, schedules are clear, and first-week travel is arranged. You check directly with each new hire rather than assuming everything is set.

jobs.title: Community Health Worker
jobs.description:
**About Us:**

Homebridge serves a high risk, high needs, complex-diagnosed population with a combination of domestic, personal, and homecare functions funded through IHSS. Our work allows an often-underserved population to live safely in their community. Homebridge offers a dynamic, fast-paced work environment with 420+ unionized field workers and 100+ internal office staff.

**Position Summary:**

The Community Health Worker (CHW) plays a vital role in improving the overall health and well-being of individuals and families in the community. They leverage their lived experiences to connect with, support, and encourage those they serve, acting as a liaison between healthcare providers, patients, and community resources. The CHW works in community settings to support underserved and vulnerable populations, helping to navigate complex systems, offer informal counseling, advocate for patient needs, and provide basic health services. They advocate on behalf of individuals by providing referrals to community-based organizations and social services that offer programming and support aligned to their needs, and complete screenings and assessments required to connect clients with appropriate services that support their health and well-being.

**Essential Duties and Responsibilities:**

Community Health Care Track

* Providing personal care and domestic support to older adults and people with disabilities facing gaps in care
* Supporting clients to connect with, engage, and navigate the health care system
* Facilitating access to appropriate medical and behavioral health support by connecting clients with appropriate clinicians, scheduling and providing accompaniment for appointments and follow ups, and supporting with medication management
* Maintaining communication between various members of the client’s Care Team

Social Work Track

* Working closely with on-site staff and other service providers supporting the client to understand their specific needs and available resources
* Identifying factors or behaviors that put the client’s holistic health (physical, mental/behavioral, social, financial, environmental, spiritual, etc) at risk and developing goals and plans in cooperation with the client to address these needs
* Designing and leading sessions that encourage development of independent living/adaptive skills such as use of public transport, inter-personal skills development, and daily living skills (cooking, cleaning, shopping, money management)
* Providing health education and sharing resources that support clients to make healthy lifestyle choices

Sustained Housing Track

* Identifying behaviors that put housing at risk and developing strategies to mitigate them.
* Educating and coaching members about behavior changes that will promote stability in housing.
* Creating and updating housing crisis plans.
* Connecting members to community and social resources to support sustained housing.
* Advocating for members with landlords and building management.

Other duties for CHWs

* Reaching out to potential clients and explaining the benefits of Homebridge services
* Assessing clients' needs and supporting the creation of a care plan with goals related to improving client’s health.
* Providing wrap-round services that improve clients' health and well-being
* Assisting clients to safely navigate transitions in care.
* Identifying and leveraging clients' strengths and support systems to promote self-management.
* Connecting with and educating client's family and social support systems to enable them to better support the client's health.
* Referring clients to social and community services that help them meet their needs and reach their goals.

**Qualifications:**

* High school diploma or equivalent required
* State-recognized CHW/P/R Certificate or at least 2000 hours/1 year of full-time work as a CHW/P/R required.
* 1–2 years’ experience in community-based or healthcare settings preferred.
* Strong computer skills, including Microsoft Office 365 and database navigation.
* English proficiency in reading, writing, and speaking required.
* Bilingual preferred but not required.
* Familiarity with local community and available resources.
* Experience with electronic medical records (EMRs) preferred.
* Ability to work independently and within a diverse, multicultural team.
* Strong organizational skills with the ability to maintain confidentiality and boundaries.

**Physical Requirements:**

* Ability to sit, stand, and walk for extended periods.
* May require occasional lifting up to 25 lbs.
* Must be able to read and interpret handwritten documents and digital information.

**Work Environment:**

* Fast-paced office and community-based environment.
* Frequent interruptions, direct client interactions, and occasional travel required.
* Work may include visits to homes, community centers, or clinics.

Homebridge is an equal opportunity employer. All applicants will be considered for employment without attention to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, veteran or disability status.

jobs.description:
**Office Manager**
==================

*Be the person who makes Hippocratic AI's fastest-growing team run like clockwork.*

**The Opportunity**
-------------------

At Hippocratic AI, our Menlo Park office is where our culture comes alive. We're looking for someone who treats the office as an experience to be crafted, not a space to be maintained: a space people genuinely want to spend time in, where small details- a stocked kitchen, a flawless event, a warm welcome at the front desk- add up to a workplace with real ambience and heart.

Many of our teams and leaders work remotely, but they come through these doors often, for all-hands, key meetings, and moments that matter, and this role makes sure they feel at home the second they walk in.

**What You'll Own**
-------------------

**The Workplace Experience.** You decide how the office runs, day to day and at scale. That means owning every vendor relationship and contract, managing budgets, and leading space planning and office moves. You keep supplies, kitchen stock, and shipping and receiving running without a hitch, and make sure the physical workplace never becomes a distraction from the work people are here to do.

**Safety, Security & Facilities Operations.** You're the first line of defense for a safe, functional workplace: overseeing building maintenance and repairs, managing badge access and visitor security, and staying ahead of health and safety compliance and emergency preparedness. When something breaks, or something's off, you're the one who notices first and gets it fixed.

**Moments That Matter.** You're the one who makes a first day, a company all-hands, team events, or the holiday party feel effortless instead of chaotic. You own event planning and execution for our headquarters, handle badge and desk setup for every new hire and contractor, keep the seating chart current as the team changes, and make sure every guest feels welcomed from the moment they arrive.

**Executive Operations.** You're a trusted extension of our G&A team: reconciling expenses with zero loose ends, booking travel well ahead of time, and managing executive visits proactively so nothing is left to chance. Some early mornings come with the territory, in service of key meetings and events.

**Location and Travel**
-----------------------

**Menlo Park office-based role:**

We believe the best ideas happen together. To support fast collaboration and a strong team culture, this role is expected to be in our Menlo Park office five days a week on a full-time basis.

**What It Takes**
-----------------

To succeed in this role, you'll need:

* Bachelor's degree required
* 7+ years of experience in office management or workplace operations within well-established corporate environments
* A track record of owning vendor and facilities relationships end-to-end, including managing a tight budget
* Experience planning and executing company-wide events
* Experience supporting senior executives with travel, expenses, or scheduling
* Multi-site office management experience required
* Flexibility to occasionally start early or travel to support executive meetings, events, or satellite offices

**Nice to have:** startup or fast-growth company experience, experience leading office moves or space planning, and experience working with flexible/managed workspace providers (e.g., WeWork).

**What Success Looks Like**
